title: Lighthill Report / AI paper symposium: evaluator anti-genealogy and contested AI-winter causal node
summary: The Lighthill Report is promoted as an anti-genealogy / evaluator-scene record rather than as a simple “AI failed” fact. The record encodes the Science Research Council commission context, Lighthill’s criticism of broad AI promise and category-B bridge work, the existence of response/commentary pieces in the paper symposium, and a historiographic caution: later historians treat its role in AI winter as important but contested and shaped by practical-problem expectations.

claims.claim: Agar 2020 says Lighthill’s criticisms have been held to be a major cause behind the dramatic slowing later called an AI winter, but argues that Lighthill’s critique was shaped by a principle of tight coupling between research and practical problem solving and by a preliminary Science Research Council steer.
what_would_change_status: A fuller historiography pass revises the causal role of the report or adds major counterinterpretations.

scope_cautions: Do not collapse evaluator critique into final truth about AI.
Do not say Lighthill alone caused AI winter without funding/historiography records.
The symposium structure matters: the report was answered by AI researchers and related scholars.
type_payload.why_it_matters_for_missing_half: It turns an oft-summarized “AI winter” anecdote into a structured anti-genealogy node: who evaluated whom, under what mandate, with what criticisms, what responses, and what contested downstream effects.

handling_notes: Represent the report as a contested policy-history source, not as humiliation of AI researchers.
Preserve response voices and the possibility that different subfields had different trajectories.
Avoid presentist scoring of 1970s expectations using 2020s systems.
